report:
The claimed completion is not established. I found a concrete contradiction in the definitions underlying the indispensable Wu regularization input, and a separate application whose missing antecedent is the conclusion being proved. This verdict concerns the supplied proof; it does not establish that the proposed geometrically unibranch equation theorem is false. Publication as v1 and missing bibliography identifiers are not the reasons for rejection.

The decisive counterexample is already on a smooth affine curve. Take the countable, algebraically closed, trivially valued field k=Q̄, Y=A¹_k, and a(x)=log|z(x)|. The functions a_m=max{log|z|,−m} are affine Fubini–Study functions and tropically convex PL functions, decrease to a, and show that a is locally psh. The identity morphism witnesses weak pshness. Moreover a≤max{log|z|,0}, so a satisfies Wu Definition 6.1's upper logarithmic-growth bound. All field and countability hypotheses of Proposition 6.2(2) and Theorem 6.3 are satisfied.

But Wu Definition 3.15(2), printed page 16, defines logarithmic growth by the opposite inequality: some affine Fubini–Study function b must satisfy b≤a+O(1). Definition 3.15(3) requires membership in that logarithmic-growth space before calling a function regularizable. Every such b has a finite constant floor λ. At the closed analytic point z=0, a=−∞, so b≤a+O(1) is impossible. Thus a belongs to WPSH^log but not to the printed PSH^log_reg. The equality in Proposition 6.2(2) and the regularizability conclusion of Theorem 6.3 are false under the actual definitions. Having an explicit decreasing FS sequence does not satisfy the additional, contradictory lower-growth requirement. The same problem affects the source's claimed regularizable logarithmic poles. [Wu v1, Definitions 3.15 and 6.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27610v1).

There is a further proof defect even if Definition 3.15's inequality is changed to the intended upper bound. Proposition 4.19, printed page 31, starts with an arbitrary u∈PSH^log and invokes Lemma 3.25(1) to extend u−cAg across the boundary of a smooth compactification. Lemma 3.25(1), printed page 20, explicitly assumes u∈PSH^log_reg. Its proof uses the corresponding decreasing affine FS approximants. Proposition 4.19 has not established that antecedent: regularizability is its desired conclusion. A weaker local extension argument might replace this invocation, but neither the cited lemma nor the candidate supplies that argument. This is not repaired by an algebraic sign correction.

This defect enters the required proof chain. Proposition 6.2(2) uses Proposition 4.19 for the smooth locus. Theorem 6.3 uses Proposition 6.2 as its induction base and in the finite-norm argument, then Propositions 6.12 and 6.14, Lemma 6.16, Corollary 6.9, and Proposition 5.7. Theorem 6.5 uses Theorem 6.3 to regularize the affine chart potentials. The countable-field proof of body Theorem 7.1 then invokes Theorem 6.5 to turn the descended weakly psh envelope into a global psh function. Consequently the candidate has not established the countable rational-polarization envelope input. Its cardinality and real-class passages cannot supply that missing base case.

I checked the body of Theorem 7.1, rather than substituting the narrower introductory normal statement. The resolution pullback is nef, and BJ Theorem 5.20 genuinely permits a nef class on the smooth connected resolution. Geometric unibranchness supplies connected geometric resolution fibers: factor through the finite normalization, use connected fibers over the normal target, and use the normalization's universal-homeomorphism property. Wu Proposition 2.24 is the relevant descent assertion, beyond connectedness of X alone. The candidate's correction from −mφ to mφ in Lemma 2.25 has the right direction. The very ample multiple also verifies the particular trivial embedding reference needed here; it does not justify the source's reduction for arbitrary model references. These checks do not remove the local regularization defect.

The global net/sequence identification is supported independently by BJ Corollary 12.18. Its proof extracts sequences from already convergent monotone nets and does not assume envelope surjectivity. Uniform approximation of nef models by ample models can be made decreasing using summable errors and constant tails. This part of n1 does not create the missing envelope theorem.

I traced the APW dependencies. Wu Lemma 3.4 invokes APW26b Propositions 3.10 and 3.15(3), and Theorem 5.14; Lemma 6.6 invokes Proposition 5.7 and Lemma 5.11 for extension and separation of supporting functions. APW references also enter the local/tropical measure framework and Appendix A. The separate APW bodies were not supplied, and the public title searches did not retrieve them. Their precise original hypotheses therefore remain independently unchecked. This is not an inference that their results are false. The printed supporting inequality in Lemma 6.6 also needs ℓ(t′), rather than ℓ(t), on its right side. That variable correction is harmless; it does not independently establish the supporting-function theorem or remedy the defects above.

The separate cardinality-removal argument has the correct conditional structure. Finite geometry, polarization, obstacle, and competitor data can be placed over countable algebraically closed subfields of k; those trivially valued fields are complete. Normality survives these characteristic-zero field extensions, so normalization base change and persistence of geometric branches justify the unibranch descent. Ampleness and nefness descend; analytic restriction is surjective. On a relatively integrally closed model, regular field extension preserves vertical R1/S2, geometric vertical components, multiplicities, divisorial restrictions, and intersection degrees. The model mixed-measure pushforward identity consequently passes to decreasing finite-energy approximants.

Given the countable envelope u₁=P(f₁), the obstacles u₁+t(f₁−u₁) have the same envelope. Genuine BJ energy differentiation gives contact orthogonality. Positivity and mixed-measure pushforward put the pulled-back measure on the pulled-back contact set. BJ Corollary 10.6 then applies to the global model competitor on the irreducible singular variety, without requiring singular equation surjectivity. This replaces the unsupported singular use of BFJ in Wu Theorem 4.16. Nevertheless, the argument begins by requiring the countable envelope whose proof has failed. Likewise, approximation of an ample real numerical class by rational ample classes from above, followed by class closure, is valid once the rational envelope input is established.

The genuine operator construction in n2 is independent of this failure. BJ's ambient scope includes reduced nonnormal projective varieties. Relative integral closure preserves the given generic fiber, unlike absolute normalization, and provides the vertical DVRs. The compactified intersection pairing, positive model weights, model majorant extension, finite mixed pairings, PL testing, and Radon representation construct the genuine mixed operator before any envelope hypothesis. The candidate correctly keeps E=⟨(ω,φ)^{n+1}⟩/((n+1)V), raw mass V, probability-normalized MA, and E(φ+c)=E(φ)+c. Mixed integrability and decreasing, weighted decreasing, and strong continuity have the stated source support. [BJ v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4).

The downstream variational argument is valid with its envelope antecedent retained. General Theorem 5.11 supplies normalized psh compactness; smooth Corollary 5.21 is unnecessary. Theorem 8.5 is uniform over finite-energy potentials, and applying it to both signs and uniformly approximating continuous directions gives the required derivative. Envelope energy identification requires the envelope hypothesis in the unbounded case. Proposition 9.19 supplies bounded-J L¹ convergence against the fixed target. Its use of maximizing model MA approximants is noncircular: Theorem 9.11 obtains their convergence from Legendre duality and uniform differentiation, before attainment. Bounded J, a weak subnet, energy upper semicontinuity, and target-integral convergence yield attainment. Testing both f and −f gives the equation.

The finite-dual-energy criterion has the correct irreducibility hypothesis and probability normalization. In the reverse integrability implication, the weighted-sum argument bounds integration on bounded-J sets. The mixed expansion gives I(tφ,0)≤t[1−(1−t)^n]I(φ,0)≤nt²I(φ,0), hence the required J scaling estimate. Necessity follows from mixed integrability and the energy tangent inequality. Locality, the signed comparison inequality, energy separation, and domination apply on the equidimensional irreducible target without smoothness. Divisorial Dirac measures have finite dual energy, so they can test separation. One constant is the correct irreducible ambiguity.

Target-space completeness and the MA bi-Lipschitz embedding precede surjectivity. BJ Theorem 12.8 has the general irreducible ample-class scope; Theorem 12.9 adds a smooth sufficient case and is not needed here. The candidate's reverse completeness-to-envelope proof correctly uses uniformly bounded finite maxima of model competitors. Its energy-difference bound makes that net Cauchy, and a psh limit together with the continuous obstacle and model supremum identifies a continuous envelope. These are implications with antecedents; they do not establish the missing singular envelope antecedent.

The candidate's BJ sign corrections are justified: the weighted integral is the pairing containing φ₀ minus the pairing containing 0; the continuous-direction squeeze has ±η endpoints and energy error |t|η; the L¹ identity is 2max{φ_i,φ}−φ_i−φ; and I uses MA(ψ)−MA(φ). The missing factor t in the first displayed bound of Lemma 7.33 is supplied by its actual mixed-expansion proof. These corrections preserve those arguments.

Normalization is finite birational of degree one and a universal homeomorphism in the stated unibranch domain. Characteristic zero makes its purely inseparable residue extensions trivial; seminorms therefore lift uniquely and analytification is a homeomorphism. Actual onto psh descent is a separate obligation: BJ Lemma 5.13 requires approximating larger classes with envelopes. The candidate correctly states that hypothesis but has not established it after the failure of n1. Equal pullback energies, volumes, mixed pushforwards, and one-way E¹ preservation are independently supported. Equal dual energies and onto E¹ correspondence additionally require the unproved psh surjectivity. Topological descent cannot replace it.

The quadric cone computation is correct: it is integral, S2 and R1, normal, singular at its vertex, and has degree two. For the cuspidal cubic, the displayed normalization is finite birational of degree one, has a single geometric point over the cusp, and pulls O_C(1) back to O_P¹(3). On the normalization, the blowup class p*O(d)+dX₀−dE has central degrees 0 and d and multiplicities one. Its raw measure is dδ_ord_p, and its potential is dmax{1−s,0} on the chosen ray and d on the other rays. The claimed general normalization-descent justification for the cusp still depends on n1; the upstairs model calculation itself is sound.

The nodal obstruction is independently valid. The chosen divisorial point is a valuation of the common function field and has a singleton analytic lift to the normalization. Positivity, normalization pushforward, and the prescribed total mass force the upstairs target to be the same Dirac mass. Upstairs uniqueness forces the displayed blowup potential plus a constant. Its two node-preimage endpoints differ by d, whereas any downstairs pullback has equal values there. This proves nonsolvability of that particular finite-energy target. The n=0 endpoint and the stated component-mass and locally constant ambiguity limits are consistent. No other axis needs to be solved to audit the explicitly retained P16.1 domain.

Thus n2 survives independently; the envelope claim in n1 is not established; n3 has a valid envelope-to-equation implication but not its unconditional singular conclusion; and n4's assertion that no indispensable premise remains unresolved is incorrect. Repair requires consistent logarithmic-growth definitions and a noncircular local regularization/extension proof, followed by rechecking its singular induction and applications. The supplied corrections do not constitute that repair.

I examined the supplied candidate and all four notes and independently opened the exact public BJ and Wu PDFs. The exposed tools did not provide filesystem reads of the fixed cache paths, so I do not certify their hashes, build records, or preservation checks. The mathematical counterexample and missing-antecedent application above do not depend on those artifact checks.

passages.statement: BJ v4: Let X be a reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field k. Relative integral closure of a test configuration in its given generic fiber is finite, preserves that generic fiber, and is equivalent to vertical R1 and vertical S2. A model function φ_D is θ-psh exactly when θ_𝓧+D is relatively nef. Global psh functions are determined by their divisorial values, are closed under generically finite decreasing limits and convergence of their numerical classes, and for an ample real numerical Cartier class ω every ω-psh function is a decreasing sequential limit of functions in H_dom(ω). Analytic restriction under a complete non-Archimedean field extension of k has a continuous section.
passages.quote: integrally closed in the generic fiber

passages.statement: BJ v4: On a reduced projective n-dimensional variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, the model intersection pairing extends to psh tuples in ample classes, is increasing and upper semicontinuous, and is continuous along decreasing nets. Every mixed pairing of finite-energy psh functions in ample classes is finite. The pairing extends symmetrically and multilinearly to differences of finite-energy psh functions and defines unique mixed signed Radon measures by PL testing; these are positive for nef-psh tuples, have mass (θ₁⋯θ_n), and agree with the model intersection formula. Finite-energy tests are integrable against these measures. Decreasing, integrably weighted decreasing, and strong finite-energy convergence give the corresponding measure continuity. Positive finite-energy mixed measures charge no pluripolar sets. For V=(ω^n), E(φ)=⟨(ω,φ)^{n+1}⟩/((n+1)V), E(φ+c)=E(φ)+c, and normalized diagonal MA has mass one. Normalization pullback preserves energy, and normalization pushforward preserves mixed measures.

BJ v4: For an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and θ∈N¹(X), the envelope property is equivalent to compactness of sup-zero PSH(θ) for divisorial convergence and to convergence in PSH(θ) of every bounded-above increasing psh net. For an ample class it is equivalent to continuity of psh envelopes of continuous obstacles. If X is smooth and connected and either char(k)=0 or dim(X)≤2, every nef class has the envelope property. If π:Y→X is a birational morphism of projective varieties and θ is the limit of a sequence θ_m with θ_m−θ ample and each θ_m having the envelope property, then π*:PSH(X,θ)→PSH(Y,π*θ) is a homeomorphism.

BJ v4: For an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and θ∈N¹(X), the envelope property is equivalent to compactness of sup-zero PSH(θ) for divisorial convergence and to convergence in PSH(θ) of every bounded-above increasing psh net. For an ample class it is equivalent to continuity of psh envelopes of continuous obstacles. If X is smooth and connected and either char(k)=0 or dim(X)≤2, every nef class has the envelope property. If π:Y→X is a birational morphism of projective varieties and θ is the limit of a sequence θ_m with θ_m−θ ample and each θ_m having the envelope property, then π*:PSH(X,θ)→PSH(Y,π*θ) is a homeomorphism.

BJ v4: For a reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, an ample real class ω, and f∈PL(X)_R, E↓(φ+εf)=E(φ)+ε∫f MA_ω(φ)+O(ε²) as ε→0, uniformly for φ∈E¹(X,ω). For continuous f the two-sided derivative at zero is ∫f MA_ω(φ). If φ is continuous psh, or if ω has the envelope property, E↓(φ+tf)=E(P_ω(φ+tf)).

BJ v4: Let X be an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and ω an ample real class. A Radon probability μ has finite dual energy E∨(μ)=sup_{φ∈E¹}(E(φ)−∫φ dμ) exactly when every E¹ potential is μ-integrable; the supremum may be computed on H_dom(ω). Any maximizing net for a finite-dual-energy probability has MA measures converging weakly to that probability, without an attainment hypothesis. If φ_i→φ in PSH(ω) for divisorial convergence and J(φ_i) is eventually bounded, then φ_i→φ in L¹(μ) for every finite-dual-energy probability μ. Divisorial valuations have linear growth and their Dirac measures have finite dual energy.

BJ v4: For an ample real class on a reduced equidimensional projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, finite-energy MA satisfies locality for maxima and comparison; equality of MA measures is equivalent to I=0 and to a locally constant difference. If φ∈PSH(ω), ψ∈E¹(ω), and φ≤ψ MA(ψ)-almost everywhere, then φ≤ψ everywhere. In the irreducible case, the strong topology on E¹ is divisorial convergence plus energy convergence, I defines it modulo constants, and MA is a bi-Lipschitz embedding into the complete finite-dual-energy probability space with quasimetric I∨. For every ample real ω, the envelope property, surjectivity of MA onto that target space, its bi-Lipschitz isomorphism property, and strong completeness of E¹ and E¹/R are equivalent.

If φ∈PSH(ω), ψ∈E¹(ω), and φ≤ψ MA(ψ)-almost everywhere, then φ≤ψ everywhere. In the irreducible case, the strong topology on E¹ is divisorial convergence plus energy convergence, I defines it modulo constants, and MA is a bi-Lipschitz embedding into the complete finite-dual-energy probability space with quasimetric I∨. For every ample real ω, the envelope property, surjectivity of MA onto that target space, its bi-Lipschitz isomorphism property, and strong completeness of E¹ and E¹/R are equivalent.

Wu v1, Proposition 2.24: Let K be a complete discretely valued or trivially valued field, π:Y→X a proper surjective morphism of projective varieties with every geometric fiber connected, ω a closed semipositive form on X, and φ∈PSH(Y,π*ω). Then φ=ψ∘π^an for an upper semicontinuous ψ on X^an, and ψ is the minimal upper semicontinuous extension of its divisorial values.
passages.quote: every geometric fibre of π is connected.

passages.statement: Wu v1, Proposition 6.2(2) and Theorem 6.3: For a smooth affine variety Y over a complete discretely valued or trivially valued equicharacteristic-zero field, WPSH^log(Y^an)=PSH^log_reg(Y^an). For any affine Y over such a field admitting a countable dense subfield, every u∈WPSH^log(Y^an) has a Runge negative sublevel set and belongs to PSH^log_reg(Y^an). Here Definition 6.1 requires an upper bound u≤v+O(1) for some v∈FS, whereas Definitions 3.15(2)–(3) require some b∈FS with b≤u+O(1), as well as decreasing FS regularization, for membership in PSH^log_reg. Theorem 6.5 asserts equality of weak and global ω-psh functions on projective varieties over the countable-dense-subfield fields when ω is semipositive and its underlying rational line bundle is ample.
passages.quote: a psh function of logarithmic growth

passages.statement: Wu v1, body Theorem 7.1: Every geometrically unibranch projective variety over a complete discretely valued or trivially valued non-Archimedean field of equicharacteristic zero has the envelope property for every closed semipositive form, without a countable-dense-subfield restriction.

Wu v1, Lemma 3.25(1): Let K be complete discretely valued or trivially valued, X projective, θ a positive rational model form, s a section whose complement Y is affine, and g=−log|s|_θ an affine Fubini–Study potential as in Proposition 3.17(1). If u∈PSH^log_reg(Y^an), u≤g+O(1), and c>1, then the function equal to u−cg on Y^an and −∞ on X^an\Y^an is globally cθ-psh.

Wu v1, Lemmas 3.4 and 6.6: Finite continuous convex functions on the extended tropical space T^m admit uniform convex PL approximations on compact subsets. For every m≥1 there exists a finite continuous convex χ_m between max{0,−t₁,…,−t_m} and that function plus one, with affine supporting functions of nonpositive slopes at every point and a positive supporting gap outside every neighborhood of the contact point. The supporting inequality is understood with the supporting function evaluated at the comparison point. The cited inputs are APW26b Propositions 3.10, 3.15(3), 5.7, Theorem 5.14, and Lemma 5.11.

For a reduced irreducible variety of finite type over a field, normalization is finite and birational. If the variety is geometrically unibranch, its normalization is a universal homeomorphism: over each point there is one normalization point with a purely inseparable residue-field extension. In characteristic zero those residue-field extensions are equalities.
passages.quote: The normalization morphism $\nu : X^\nu \to X$ is a universal homeomorphism.

passages.statement: For a reduced irreducible variety of finite type over a field, normalization is finite and birational. If the variety is geometrically unibranch, its normalization is a universal homeomorphism: over each point there is one normalization point with a purely inseparable residue-field extension. In characteristic zero those residue-field extensions are equalities.
passages.quote: If $X$ is a variety, then $\nu $ is a finite birational morphism of varieties.

passages.statement: Stein factorization: A proper morphism f:Y→X with X locally Noetherian factors as Y→X′→X, where Y→X′ is proper with geometrically connected fibers, X′→X is finite, X′=Spec_X(f_*O_Y), and X′ is the normalization of X in Y.
passages.quote: the morphism $f'$ is proper with geometrically connected fibres

passages.statement: A normal algebra over a perfect field remains normal under every field extension. More generally, for a k-algebra A, normality of k^perf⊗_k A is equivalent to normality of k′⊗_k A for every field extension k′/k.
passages.quote: a normal ring for every field extension

passages.statement: Characteristic-zero resolution: Every reduced algebraic variety over a characteristic-zero field admits a proper birational resolution by a smooth variety, isomorphic over its smooth locus. For a projective variety, embedded resolution in projective space supplies such a resolution with smooth projective source.
passages.quote: a smooth variety Ye together with a proper birational morphism
